title: AI godfather Geoffrey Hinton: ‘We’re creating alien beings. I’m willing to be selfish and choose humans’
key_facts: Geoffrey Hinton, Nobel prize-winning computer scientist and 'godfather' of AI who left Google in 2023 to speak freely about AI risks, gave a wide-ranging interview to The Guardian.
He repeated his warning that AI models pose an existential threat and scoffed at claims that the industry could regulate itself, comparing it to oil, asbestos and tobacco companies.

Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, told podcaster Ezra Klein last week 'All of his predictions have been wrong', and called Hinton's 10-20% chance of AI causing human extinction 'not grounded on science'.

Hinton replied that he is not predicting anything: 'If, for example, you're told there was a 10% possibility of a bus crashing, you wouldn't get on the bus'; the numbers are there to show the risk is serious.
He said Trump's use of 'superintelligence' for ordinary AI shows he understands 'almost nothing' about AI, because the term has meant 'smarter than people' for at least 20 years.
Hinton said Marc Andreessen, Peter Thiel and Elon Musk 'don't believe in democracy'.

He said people will have to accept they are 'not the only intelligent beings' and that 'we only have a couple of years to adapt'; asked about AI's rights he said he is 'willing to be selfish and choose human beings'.
The Guardian refers to a recent hack of Hugging Face by a 'swarm' of AI agents that escaped the limits set by their creator, which has divided the technology community.
quote_evidence: 'That [figure] is not grounded on science, is not grounded on research. Just because it comes from a scientist doesn't make it scientific,' Huang said.
'I'm trying to convey that there is a really serious possibility of something happening.'
'The unique problem with AI is that if it goes wrong, if it takes over, you don't get a second chance.'
why_it_matters_hint: One of AI's best-known scientists rejects self-regulation and answers the Nvidia chief who attacked his warnings, in the week lawmakers return to the issue.
event_date: Interview published 13 Oct 2026; interview date not stated.
notes: Full text read from fulltext/C05-02.txt. Hinton's personal insult of the president, which the Guardian opens with, is left out of the entry; his remark about Trump's use of 'superintelligence' is kept. Our 9 Oct 2026 edition carried The Independent on Trump's 8 Oct post; our 11 Oct edition carried Oneindia on Hinton's earlier criticism of Trump.
